messages.content: What does `sub` mean in Exsecutor?

`sub` is a reserved word in group "capability" (§8.4, tier 1). Latin: sub, 'under'. Role: Binds a capability provider for a scope: `sub ambitus = a;` to the end of the scope, or a block form (§4.5). The provider must have the atom's own capability type (`EXS-E0303` otherwise), and binding one atom twice in a scope is `EXS-E0422`. English analogue: none; a scoped dependency binding. Being reserved, it is never usable as an identifier anywhere: `firma sub: u8 = 1;` is `EXS-E0220` (checked with `exsc`).
What does `quisque` mean in Exsecutor?

`quisque` is a reserved word in group "iteration" (§8.4, tier 1). Latin: quisque, 'each one'. Role: The independent loop, `quisque i in 0..n { ... }`: iterations do not observe one another and their order is unspecified. No dependency analysis exists, so today it is a trusted assertion `[OPEN]` (§8.5). English analogue: none; a parallel for-each. Being reserved, it is never usable as an identifier anywhere: `firma quisque: u8 = 1;` is `EXS-E0220` (checked with `exsc`).
Is `licentia` a reserved word in Exsecutor?

No. `licentia` is a contextual keyword (§8.4, tier 2: `ego`-file structure): The licence entry of an `ego` file, `licentia "LGPL-3.0-or-later"` (§10.1). Everywhere else it is an ordinary identifier, so `firma licentia: u8 = 1;` is accepted by `exsc` (checked). Latin/gloss: licentia, 'licence'. `[UNTESTED]`: the CST parses no `ego` block yet, so this word's contextual status in an `ego` file is the grammar's claim and nothing has measured it (§8.4).
Is `rotundatio` a reserved word in Exsecutor?

No. `rotundatio` is a contextual keyword (§8.4, tier 2: `numeri` keys and values): A `numeri` key: the rounding mode, default `ad_parem` (§5.4). Everywhere else it is an ordinary identifier, so `firma rotundatio: u8 = 1;` is accepted by `exsc` (checked). Latin/gloss: rotundatio, 'rounding'.
Is `subnormales` a reserved word in Exsecutor?

No. `subnormales` is a contextual keyword (§8.4, tier 2: `numeri` keys and values): A `numeri` key: subnormal handling, default `conservata`, meaning no flush-to-zero (§5.4). Everywhere else it is an ordinary identifier, so `firma subnormales: u8 = 1;` is accepted by `exsc` (checked). Latin/gloss: subnormales, 'subnormals'.
Is `et` a reserved word in Exsecutor?

No. `et` is a contextual keyword (§8.4, tier 2: comparison and connectives): Short-circuit conjunction (§8.6 level 8). Everywhere else it is an ordinary identifier, so `firma et: u8 = 1;` is accepted by `exsc` (checked). Latin/gloss: et, 'and'.
Is `deorsum` a reserved word in Exsecutor?

No. `deorsum` is a contextual keyword (§8.4, tier 2: exclusive or and shifts): Shift down (right); non-associative (§5.4, §8.6 level 5a). Everywhere else it is an ordinary identifier, so `firma deorsum: u8 = 1;` is accepted by `exsc` (checked). Latin/gloss: deorsum, 'downward'.
Is `else` a keyword in Exsecutor?

No. `else` is not an Exsecutor keyword, so it is an ordinary identifier: you may declare a name spelled `else`, and until you do, using it is `EXS-E0301` (name does not resolve). The reserved set is the thirty Latin words of §8.4 (plus the contextual words), and none of them is English apart from `dyn`. The Exsecutor spelling of the common words is: `if` -> `si`, `else if` -> `sin`, `else` -> `aliter`, `while` -> `dum` (with a `terminus` bound), `for` -> `per` or `quisque`, `return` -> `redde`, `let`/`const` -> `firma`, `let mut` -> `mutabilis`, `fn` -> `functio`, `struct` -> `structura`. There is no boolean literal: a truth value is the one-bit type `u1`, written 1 and 0.

What does `( )` mean in Exsecutor?
`( )`: parameter lists, argument lists, grouping (§8.4 "Operators and sigils"; first shown in §4.2).
What does `,` mean in Exsecutor?
`,`: separator (§8.4 "Operators and sigils"; first shown in §4.2).
What is the capability `sermo`?

`sermo` is a capability atom (§4.6, §8.4 tier 3) — human language. Capability atoms are identifiers in the capability namespace, not reserved words. Capability types are unforgeable: no literal, no cast, no default. The only root is the `Mundus` passed to `initium`; every other capability is derived from it explicitly (§4.1).
What does the diagnostic `EXS-E0103` mean?
`EXS-E0103` means: bidi or invisible control character in source. Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.
What does the diagnostic `EXS-E0202` mean?
`EXS-E0202` means: unterminated construct. Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.
What does the diagnostic `EXS-E0307` mean?
`EXS-E0307` means: control flow misuse. Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.
What does the diagnostic `EXS-E0322` mean?
`EXS-E0322` means: implicit padding in a `@transitus` type. Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.

`EXS-E0423` means: capability row item malformed. Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.
What does the diagnostic `EXS-E0510` mean?

`EXS-E0510` means: capability escapes a declared bound (trait ceiling or `dyn`). Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.

`EXS-E0520` means: non-atomic `refero` crossing `externus`. Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.

`EXS-E0812` means: generic does not monomorphize within the closure under `profilum certum`. Codes are permanent and tools match codes, never English prose (§8.3); the wording of the message may change, the code never will.

Derive the family of names from the Exsecutor root `iung-`.

Root `iung-` (supine `iunct-`), "join" (§3.3). Applying §3.4's suffixes to the right stem:

- `iunctor` — agent `structura`, takes the supine stem
- `iungibilis` — can-be-Xed `interfacies`, takes the present stem
- `iunctio` — reified operation `structura`, takes the supine stem
- `iunctus` — result `typus`, takes the supine stem
- `iunctorium` — instrument `structura`, takes the supine stem

The `-e` action form is a morphological category, not a spelling — the imperative of this root is not given by the spec's table, since Latin realises it differently by conjugation (`-e` in the third, `-a` in the first: `lege`, `plica`, `saluta`). This is derived mechanically from §3.3-§3.5's tables, which the spec itself says are illustrative and not the morpheme table (`lexicon.norma` does not exist yet). The checker's lexicon pass (`EXS-E0601`-`EXS-E0603`, `EXS-E0610`) is built and tested against hand-built trees and is not enabled in the driver, so no compiler run backs this. `[UNTESTED]`
What does the Exsecutor prefix `in-` mean?

`in-` means "into" and carries this signature law: first parameter is the destination type (§3.5). Violating a prefix law is `EXS-E0603`. Prefix laws constrain `functio` signatures only; on a `structura`, `typus` or `interfacies` a prefix is positional and semantic.
Can a domain such as linear algebra have its own Exsecutor lexicon?

Yes. `lexicon.norma` holds the core, and a specialised domain may carry its own separately hashed and separately depended-upon table, such as `lexicon.algebra` or `lexicon.rete`, so a program that never touches the domain does not inherit its vocabulary. Sub-lexicons obey §3.9 in full; they are not a relaxation (§3.9.6). `exsc lexicon` is the intended checker and is a stub today `[OPEN]` (§3.9.7).
How does `sub` work, and what stops it minting a capability?

`sub P = e;` binds the provider `e` as the scope's one value of capability `P` until the end of the scope; there is also a block form. Resolution is lexical and non-searching: one value per capability type per scope, shadowing is an error (`EXS-E0422`), and there is no implicit conversion. Because `sub` is the one statement that mints an atom, its provider must have the atom's own capability type, or it is `EXS-E0303`: `sub ambitus = m.ambitus();` is fine, `sub archivum = d;` with `d: Directorium` is not. The one exemption is `alloc`, whose provider has no named type yet `[OPEN]` (§4.5).
What is the difference between `refero<T>` and `refero_communis<T>`?

`refero<T>` is a non-atomic reference-counted reference and cannot cross an `externus` boundary (`EXS-E0520`); `refero_communis<T>` is atomic and may cross. A foreign thread racing a non-atomic refcount is a use-after-free that the type system cannot see (§6.4). The refcount is 64-bit on every target, and the retain that would carry out of 64 bits aborts rather than saturating (§6.5).
What does it take to build the Exsecutor compiler?

Exactly one tool: `fasmg`, plus the vendored x86-64 macro package under `vendor/fasmg-x86` (§18.1). `make` builds `build/exsc` from `compiler/x86_64/exsc.asm`. `exsc aedifica --hospes x86_64-linux SOURCE...` type-checks the files named as one compilation unit; with `-o OUT` it lowers and emits fasmg source (the reference backend), which `fasmg OUT BIN` assembles. `--emitte c` selects the C backend. `--hospes` is required, since an absent target is an error rather than a default (§9.5). Only `aedifica` does anything today; the other subcommands exit 4 `[OPEN]`.
Name a set of capabilities once and require it in a function's row.
A `potestas` is a named capability set, and it can stand in the row: `poscit Hospes` requires everything `Hospes` lists. This is ergonomics only: the audit still reads the expanded set.

Show Exsecutor's three overflow behaviours for u8 addition.

Overflow is a property of the operator, not a compiler flag. Plain `+` traps on overflow, `+%` wraps modulo 2^N, `+|` saturates. The same three spellings exist for subtraction (`-`, `-%`, `-|`). `circum(100)` is 44 and `satura(100)` is 255.
Write a program whose exit status is the 10th Fibonacci number, computed with a bounded `dum` loop.

`dum i lt n terminus 100` loops while the condition holds and declares a bound of 100 entries; the bound is evaluated once and exceeding it aborts. `firma t` inside the loop is a fresh immutable binding per iteration, used to swap without a temporary variable that outlives the step.

It returns exit status 55. I compiled it with `exsc`, assembled it with `fasmg` and ran it to confirm.

Add 200 to 100 as u8 with the plain `+` operator.

Plain `+` is the trapping operator: 100 + 200 does not fit a `u8`, so the program aborts. A trap is observable in exactly one shape, `abortus N` on fd 2 followed by `SIGILL`, because `initium -> u8` makes every exit status a legitimate result and so none can be reserved for failure. Choose `+%` to wrap or `+|` to saturate if overflow is expected.

It aborts rather than returning a status: it writes `abortus 1` to standard error and is killed by `SIGILL`, the one observable shape of a runtime abort (§6.6). I compiled it, assembled it with `fasmg` and ran it to confirm.

Build an array of four u32 values from a literal and sum it with a loop.

`[e1, …, en]` is an array literal of type `acies<T, n>`; `N` is part of the type. `[e; N]` repeats one value N times (the way to ask for zeros, since nothing is zero-filled). In `per i in 0..4`, a range of two literals types as `mensura`, which is what indexes an array.
Declare a little-endian wire header: a 16-bit magic, a byte, and a 32-bit payload length.

`:minor` is little-endian and `:maior` big-endian; both are contextual words. Each multi-byte field names its order, and the struct is packed with no padding, so this header is seven bytes on the wire: 2 + 1 + 4.
Declare a one-byte wire header holding two 4-bit fields, version and kind.

Sub-byte fields `u1`–`u7` pack MSB-first in declaration order, so `versio` takes the high nibble. A field wider than 8 bits must begin on a byte boundary and be a whole number of bytes (`u12` does not parse), and the declared widths must sum to a whole number of bytes: a lone `u4` is implicit padding, EXS-E0322. A byte-order suffix on a sub-byte field does not parse (`u4:maior` is EXS-E0201).
